summary: I fluid motion contrasts with III causative shedding: liquid is I subject but III zero-marked object; the affected source is m-marked in both.
Water appears with singular-shaped xayər in2/23 and plural Infectum at2/45,94/131. This is agreement evidence, not a second flow sense.
xār/xōr contractions are copied from the MAC edition; the supplied plain/emphatic spellings are retained. The older xayro sweat example is already in the Infectum box.
III already exists in the entry and quotes the Dawid promise in its sense field. Adding a regular box repairs structure; it does not establish a new stem or new lexical meaning.
Single-sense inherited unlabelled examples are counted under implicit1.
Round-1 III form-order and misplaced-quotation repairs are used in the human baseline only; they are not repeated in round-2 JSON.
I.1 retains fluids and granular outflow. I.2 adds human motion along a watercourse; the participant change also entails a different posture/motion event.
The omen’s future blood flow is inside reported belief, not a separate prophetic lexical sense. No III or Detransitive occurrence is added here.
MAC Xalaf23: is the flowing subject the basin, its water or their combined contents? Keep the proposed extension conditional.
The existing III story citation ends [269 NE Story of Dawid3:24], while the supplied verse is MAC NE Story of Dawid/16. Check edition/version numbering before changing the inherited citation.
PrS26/14 appears to be the same leg/blood/pus quotation cited as prs63/16; verify numbering. Masculine Xayər with feminine quantity noun dəgušto may agree with contents.
90/155: confirm basket/container antecedent of feminine xayiro; the provided line leaves it implicit.
Confirm whether xyr in Jan 2.4/794 can describe sliding on other surfaces or specifically water-assisted sliding; the single attestation does not establish that range.
Container-for-contents subjects are possible at90/155 and MAC Xalaf23; the latter could instead refer to water alone. No autonomous drift/leak sense is established.
